item.description: NettZero’s longevity lies in its ability to anticipate and respond to the evolving sustainability demands, staying ahead of industry shifts, and delivering practical high-impact solutions for clients.

item.description: There’s a whole science to the art of creating strong brand impact at the best of times. In a world that’s challenged by tough business conditions if you’re trying to push out a green product or service you need to hit the right mark first time.

item.title: Do you need to measure your carbon emissions, understand your energy use, and optimise that use? Here’s how Wattwatchers can help - The Green List
item.description: There are now more than 50,000 Wattwatchers devices out in the field across Australia and the world. It started out by offering accurate and cost effective solar installation measurements.

item.description: If it’s been 10 years since you last thought about updating your HVAC system, it’s probably time for an upgrade, said Sam Ringwaldt, founder and chief executive of Conry Tech.

item.title: Elumen: How to make sure your emergency lighting is best in class for technology, safety and sustainability - The Green List
item.description: When a shopping centre in Sydney’s inner west was repeatedly outed for poor fire and safety standards, the story eventually hit the headlines. It’s the kind of care and concern that has propelled Elumen to think best in class for safety.

item.title: Grand net zero aspirations, and don’t know where to start? Eco-Ms is here to help - The Green List
item.description: When a council, school or hotel calls Eco-MS, it’s rarely just about a broken chiller. On paper, the brief is simple: improve comfort, cut costs, and hit net zero targets. In reality, the building is a maze of legacy plant, patchy commissioning and competing priorities.

item.title: Forgot your reusable cup? No problem: Why office buildings and cafes are turning to Cercle - The Green List
item.description: Cercle is a free-to-use, reusable coffee cup system and network in Australia, focusing on commercial spaces. While many businesses want to integrate circular principles, BYO initiatives often fail because people simply forget their reusable cups.

item.title: Fast growth in new Aussie turf for AESG - The Green List
item.description: In less than 12 months AESG has gone from kick starting its Australian operations, headed by Devan Valenti in Sydney and Douglas Sum in Melbourne, to a staff of 11 in Australia and more than 15 across Australia and Southeast Asia.
